sections.title: What you see
paragraphs: An endpoint is one side of a connection: a serial port, a TCP client or listener, a folder or an SFTP server. Each row is one line: its kind and address, its state and how long it has lasted, bytes in and out and last activity, and when there is room the failure streak, the channels that use it and its last error. Text that does not fit ends in an ellipsis and shows whole when you point at it; on a narrow window columns drop from the right, starting with Last error.

sections.title: What to do
paragraphs: Find an endpoint by name, address or channel, and filter by kind or state. Open one to see which channel holds it, its peer, the next retry and the last error. Add endpoint in the page header opens the editor (see Endpoint editor help). States help explains the states.
